kind: iPad, Windows, and what you asked for
title: iPad, Windows, and what you asked for
blurb: Purify comes to the iPad properly and to Windows for the first time, and most of the rest was asked for in the app's own Community tab: liking a reply, a way to undo a block, a way to keep a saint close at hand. Prayer and Discover are redone, the Bible gains 2 Esdras, you choose which email you get from us, and likes that had not been saving now do. And Purify Plus now asks for the subscription it always described, while the Scriptures, the saints, the prayers and the calendar stay free.
items: Like a reply. Replies in Community can now be liked, as posts can. You asked for this twice, and the last release said it had shipped. For replies it had not; now it has.
Undo a block. Blocking someone now asks first, and Account, then Security, lists the readers you have blocked, each with an Unblock button. A block now hides their replies as well as their posts.
Pinned announcements. Notes from the Purify team can now sit at the top of the Community feed.
Verified accounts now show their badge beside their name in Community. The badge had been granted, but the feed had nowhere to show it.

Your email, your choice. Two optional lists, What is new in the library and New in the shop, stay off until you turn them on in Settings, under Notifications. Either can be stopped from the email itself, and every email from us now wears the app's own look.

Name days. Choose a patron saint in the same place, and on the morning of their feast a short note about them arrives, with a link to their life in the library. It comes with the library list, so turn that on as well.

items.text: Likes in Community now save every time, and a post you have liked shows as liked when you come back. Before, a like could fail to save, and pressing a like the app had forgotten took it away.
Your name on your profile now saves. The editor could sit on Saving and keep the old name.
Prayers before Communion showed a line of code where its name belonged. It has its name now, in every language.
The app's tab bar fits every label on smaller phones and in narrow iPad windows, where Community used to be cut short.
In the app, closing the payment window without paying no longer leaves an order behind. You stay where you were.
The release notes inside the app now match the ones on the website.
On the Light palette, cards and buttons drawn for the dark palettes stayed dark, with dark writing on them. They follow Light now, on every page.

The readings on the Bible tab now say that they are for the day's saints and feasts, as they are on most days, and the calendar says plainly that the daily course of readings is not in Purify yet. A reader asked why ours differed from a church calendar; that is why.
Settings is in your language all the way through. The reader's font, size, interlinear and calendar choices had stayed in English.
The bar across the top of the website fits every screen. On smaller laptops it ran past the right edge, and in longer languages it turns into a menu button wherever the links do not fit.
In the reader's settings, the Purify Plus label no longer sits on top of the names Candlelight and Monastery.
Your initials now sit in a plain circle, the same everywhere your account appears, and a one-word name shows one letter instead of two.

Purify on iPad. The app now fills the iPad screen in either orientation, with its own tab bar, and works beside other apps in Split View, Slide Over and Stage Manager. Android tablets keep their navigation too: held upright, they used to show none.

Purify for Windows. On a Windows computer, the front page of purifyapp.net offers it under Open Purify: the prayers, the Scriptures with the Fathers, the saints and the calendar in a window of their own. It can also show your friends on Discord your patron saint, a line from a favorite saint, or what you are reading, and it stays off until you turn it on.
Save a saint. A Save button on every saint's page keeps them in Saved, so you can go straight back. For now, saints are kept on the device you saved them on.
Candlelight is now black and light grey instead of warm amber, and still dimmer than the Dark palette for late-hour reading.
The large first letter of each chapter now follows your palette. On Light it was a pale gold that was hard to read; now it is clear on every palette.
2 Esdras is in the Bible, all sixteen chapters. It is not in the Greek Septuagint, so it is read in the King James Version of 1769.

Susanna, Bel and the Dragon, the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three can be found by name, in every language. They were always here, inside Daniel as the Septuagint keeps them, and Daniel now shows where each begins.
Discover is new. It opens on where to begin, with History, Reading and the saints, and gathers theology, the councils and the calendar in one place to study the faith.
The front page now shows Purify on iPhone, iPad and Android, with both stores' ratings and the app rising into view as you scroll.

Prayer is redone. It opens on four prayers for right now: the one you left off, then what fits the hour, the season and the fast. The whole prayer book follows by category, with every prayer under its own name.
Choosing a patron saint is a search now: type any part of a name, with or without accents, instead of scrolling a list of 158.
Tell me when it is back. A sold-out piece now offers one email when it returns. Sign in to use it.
When your order ships, we email you the tracking number and a link to follow the parcel, and after it arrives, a short guide to caring for an icon or a prayer rope.

Each piece now shows how many other people have it in their cart this week, and how many are left once five or fewer remain, with rows for pieces that go well with your cart and pieces you looked at recently.

Purify Plus now does what it says. Candlelight and Monastery, your own collections and the Florilegium, Immersive History and sync across devices are part of Plus on the website and on Android: you can see each one, and tapping it tells you so. The Scriptures, the saints, the prayers, the calendar and the history itself stay free for everyone.

A small gold cross now sits beside the names of Purify Plus members in Community, inside a thin red ring for Pro. It is a mark and nothing more, with no weight in the feed, and members can turn it off in their account settings.
In the Windows app, Plus members can frame their Discord portrait in the color of the church's season, with a thin gold rule if they like.
The library now holds 158 saints and 78 books of Scripture: 1,362 chapters and 36,667 verses.
